title: Dynamic Probability Model Parameter Adjustment
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic probability model parameter adjustment algorithm designed to enhance model accuracy on specific datasets. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often employ fixed parameters, limiting the algorithm's ability to adapt to the data. We propose a dynamic approach, termed "Dynamic Probability Parameter Adjustment," that learns and automatically adjusts model parameters based on the data itself. This adaptive learning process significantly improves predictive performance compared to static parameter adjustments. The core mechanism of this algorithm centers on iteratively refining model parameters through a feedback loop, allowing the model to converge towards optimal performance. This work explores the benefits of this adaptive approach and its potential impact on various probabilistic modeling applications.

abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm for constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) designed to dynamically adjust constraints during the search process. Traditional CSP solvers often rely on static constraints, limiting their ability to effectively explore the solution space. This work introduces a reinforcement learning agent that learns optimal constraint adjustments, thereby enabling a more adaptive and potentially more efficient search strategy. We explore the implementation of this agent within a quantum framework and demonstrate its effectiveness on a benchmark CSP. The core mechanism centers around a quantum state representation and a reinforcement learning algorithm optimized for constraint transformation. The resulting algorithm offers a potential advancement over static approaches by incorporating continuous, adaptive constraint manipulation.

title: Quantum Adaptive Topology Algorithm Acceleration
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm, the Quantum Adaptive Topology Algorithm Acceleration (QATA), designed to accelerate quantum algorithms through dynamic adjustments of quantum topology. Traditional quantum algorithm acceleration relies heavily on classical optimization, while QATA leverages a fundamentally different approach – a core algorithm that actively shapes the quantum state to optimize performance. The core mechanism of QATA involves a dynamically evolving topology, allowing for a more flexible and efficient exploration of quantum solutions. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating significant speedups for a range of quantum algorithms, particularly those exhibiting complex topological phases. We discuss the implications of this approach for the future of quantum computing.

title: Non-Linear Matrix Dynamics Theory
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic mapping theory for non-linear matrices, aiming to facilitate machine learning algorithms through automated matrix adaptation and optimization. We propose a framework where the matrix's dynamic evolution is modeled as a physical process, allowing for learning and control of this evolution. The core mechanism focuses on establishing a dynamic mapping between the matrix's initial state and its subsequent states, leveraging techniques from dynamical systems and reinforcement learning to achieve optimal performance. This theory offers a promising alternative to traditional machine learning approaches, particularly in situations where data scarcity or complex dynamics are prevalent. This work demonstrates the potential of this approach to enhance the performance of machine learning models across various applications.

title: Разработка алгоритмов планирования траектории для автономных мобильных роботов на основе глубокого обучения с подкреплением
abstract: Цель данной работы — создание алгоритма планирования траекторий без использования карт для автономных мобильных роботов, действующих в незнакомых средах, с использованием методов глубокого обучения с под-креплением (DRL). Проверка была сосредоточена на методах навигации на основе DRL, работающих без знания о среде или ее предварительно созданной карты. В работе были поставлены и решены следующие пять задач: 1. Обзор современных подходов DRL для навигации роботов; 2. Разработка метода планирования траектории без карты на основе алгоритма Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) с использованием необработанных данных сенсоров; 3. Реализация предложенного метода в симуляционной среде ROS 2–Gazebo; 4. Оценка показателей успешности выполнения задачи, способности к обобщению и вычислительной эффективности. В результате работы был создан функциональный агент DRL, способный осуществлять навигацию в сложных, ранее неизвестных средах, содержащих как статические, так и динамические препятствия. Агент достигает показателя успешности выполнения задачи свыше 95% при работе в реальном времени. Полученные результаты демонстрируют, что сквозной подход к навигации на основе DRL с использованием SAC представляет собой надежную и экономичную по количеству обучающих примеров альтернативу традиционным модульным системам навигации. Результаты данного исследования могут способствовать разработке решений для автономной навигации в таких приложениях, как складская логистика, операции по поиску и спасению, а также сервисная робототехника в неотображённых или неструктурированных средах.

title: O Cerrado stricto sensu na perspectiva da Educação Matemática Inventiva
abstract: O Cerrado apresenta grande diversidade de fitofisionomias, entre as quais o Cerrado stricto sensu se destaca por representar uma das formações savânicas mais características do bioma. Apesar de sua relevância ecológica, estudantes da Educação Básica frequentemente apresentam dificuldades em compreender as relações que caracterizam essa fitofisionomia. Nesse contexto, este estudo teve como objetivo analisar as compreensões produzidas por estudantes sobre o Cerrado stricto sensu durante seu percurso inventivo em uma experiência de Educação Matemática Inventiva com Robótica Educacional, mediada por um livro interativo. O artigo integra uma série de seis estudos, cada um dedicado à análise das compreensões produzidas em um dos módulos do livro interativo sobre as fitofisionomias do Cerrado. A pesquisa, de abordagem qualitativa, foi desenvolvida na perspectiva da pesquisa-intervenção cartográfica. O Produto Educacional Robótica Educacional no Cerrado foi constituído a partir de experiências realizadas com 69 estudantes do 7º ano, em 2024, que colaboraram na composição de mundos inventivos por meio da construção de maquetes, da montagem e programação de robôs educacionais e da produção de vídeos. Posteriormente, o livro interativo foi compartilhado com 33 estudantes do 7º ano, em 2025. O presente estudo analisa as compreensões produzidas pelo grupo de quatro estudantes responsável pelo módulo que investiga o Cerrado stricto sensu, acompanhadas por meio das respostas às questões investigativas e do registro reflexivo elaborado ao final da experiência. A análise evidenciou quatro movimentos analíticos: produção de compreensões iniciais sobre o Cerrado stricto sensu; identificação e classificação do Cerrado stricto sensu; produção de compreensões sobre as características ecológicas do Cerrado stricto sensu; e registro reflexivo e produção de sentidos sobre o percurso inventivo. Os resultados indicam que a articulação entre o livro interativo, a Robótica Educacional, os vídeos, as maquetes e as questões investigativas favoreceu a produção de compreensões sobre o Cerrado stricto sensu. Além disso, a análise evidenciou potencialidades do próprio Produto Educacional, ao indicar a necessidade de reformulação de uma das questões investigativas para favorecer produções mais autorais, interpretativas e problematizadoras. Conclui-se que a articulação entre Ensino de Ciências, Educação Matemática Inventiva e Robótica Educacional evidencia potencialidades para o desenvolvimento de experiências investigativas sobre as fitofisionomias do Cerrado na Educação Básica

title: PRICE: A Systematic Study of LLM Adaptation Choices for Bitcoin Price Forecasting
abstract: Cryptocurrency markets exhibit extreme volatility and non-stationary dynamics that challenge conventional forecasting methods. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise for time series forecasting, the combined effects of adaptation choices remain largely unexplored in financial settings. This study introduces PRICE, a structured approach for adapting LLMs to short-term Bitcoin price forecasting. Built on a 4-bit quantized LLaMA-3 8B model, PRICE investigates how fine-tuning, numerical representation, prompting, inference, and decoding jointly influence forecasting performance. PRICE integrates Parameter-efficient fine-tuning with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), Recursive multi-step inference, Integer-rounded numerical representation, Context-Task-Format (CTF) prompting, and Exact zero-temperature decoding. Ablation studies show that each component contributes to forecasting accuracy and reliability. LoRA enables efficient training on limited hardware, recursive inference improves accuracy, integer-rounded values reduce errors, CTF prompting outperforms Chain-of-Thought, Implicit Chain-of-Thought (iCoT), and few-shot prompting, and zero-temperature decoding improves stability during recursive forecasting. Comparative evaluation against eight transformer-based and time-series foundation models shows that PRICE achieves the lowest forecasting errors on both validation and test sets while maintaining robust performance across evaluation periods. Despite being based on a model primarily pretrained on text rather than time-series data, PRICE achieves competitive or superior performance relative to specialized foundation models. These findings demonstrate that adaptation choices critically determine the accuracy and robustness of LLMs for numerical time-series forecasting.

title: VICAL: Vicinal Consistency Alignment for Long-Tailed Visual Recognition
abstract: Multi-expert models have become the dominant paradigm for long-tailed learning, largely attributed to their presumed ability to benefit from expert diversity. However, we revisit this central assumption and reveal that diversity induced by logit adjustment or explicit regularizers does not guarantee better ensemble accuracy. Our work suggests that multi-expert models benefit more from variance reduction than diversity maximization. We introduce \textbf{VICAL}, a \textbf{VI}cinal \textbf{C}onsistency \textbf{AL}ignment framework that improves long-tailed recognition not by enforcing expert diversity, but by reducing prediction variance. Specifically, our approach comprises two key components: Self-Consistency Learning and Deep Ensemble Distillation. Self-Consistency Learning discourages reliance on unstable high-frequency information, smoothing the local loss landscape and mitigating overfitting, especially for tail classes. Deep Ensemble Distillation promotes cross-expert low-frequency semantic agreement using a low-resolution view, thereby sidestepping optimization conflicts with established knowledge. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-LT, ImageNet-LT, and iNaturalist 2018 show that VICAL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, validating the effectiveness of our consistency-driven design. Our code is available at \href{https://github.com/FlamieZhu/Vicinal-Consistency-Alignment}{VICAL}.

title: Compiling Quantum Regular Language States
abstract: Artifact for Accepted Paper #331: "Compiling Quantum Regular Language States" (OOPSLA 2026) arXiv: 2602.02698 A quantum state-preparation compiler for Regular Language States (RLS). Users describe target states via regular expressions, bitstring lists, or DFAs, and the compiler produces hardware-aware quantum circuits via two backends: SeqRLSP (linear depth, LNN connectivity) and TreeRLSP (logarithmic depth, all-to-all connectivity). Getting started and verifying the results: Download all files into a single directory tar xzf rlscomp-artifact.tar.gz cd rlscomp-artifact docker load < docker-image.tar docker run --platform linux/amd64 -it -v $(pwd):/work rlscomp-artifact bash python run_sec56_sec57.py (sanity check, ~1 min) See README.md for full instructions and CLAIMS.md for the mapping of paper claims to experiments. Reusing the code: To reuse and build upon the code please refer to the additional resources: Document What it covers ARCHITECTURE.md High-level overview of the codebase: the four-stage compilation pipeline, a module-by-module map, the data representations and conventions every stage relies on, a table mapping each construction in the paper to the function that implements it, and an annotated end-to-end trace of one compilation. GUIDE.md Guide to the main functionality: installation, the four ways to describe a state, complements, choosing between the three backends, verifying that a circuit is correct, measuring circuit cost the way the paper does, exporting circuits, using the intermediate stages directly, running benchmark sweeps, and a troubleshooting table. EXTENDING.md Applying and extending the package beyond our experiments: adding input front ends, compiling states that are not regular languages, adding methods to the benchmark harness, adding new circuit backends, generalising past the binary alphabet, using the analysis machinery on its own, known limits with workarounds, and how to test an extension.

title: The Detroja Cyclic Research Model: Quantum Hardware Execution, Technical Benchmarks, and Comparative Analysis Report
abstract: This report details the empirical research, technical benchmarks, and comparative performance analysis of The Detroja Cyclic Research Model executed on real 156-qubit quantum hardware (IBM Quantum Heron) and evaluated against global Non-Equilibrium Quantum Field Dynamics (NEQFD) theory benchmarks. It covers hardware benchmarks, quantum noise and error analysis, cross-platform architecture readiness using Python Cirq for Google Quantum processors, and optimized execution modules.

title: Georacoon - testing and example dataset
abstract: This dataset provides geographic raster datasets (GeoTIFF) used as example and test data forthe GeoRacoon Python package. None of this data is shipped with the installed package, it exists for contributors and example scripts working from a git clone, fetched on demand. All source datasets are third-party data, redistributed here under their own upstreamlicenses (not GeoRacoon's own MIT code license). Per-dataset provenance and licensedetail below. Alterations: reprojected from the Sinusoidal version in examples/ to EPSG:2056 (Swiss LV95). switzerland_ndvi-binned-mean_2015_LANDSAT-8_epsg3035.tifLandsat-8 composite, 2015. title: 自适应量子态的动态能量控制
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum state control centered around dynamic energy modulation. We propose a self-adaptive algorithm that intelligently adjusts key quantum parameter values, specifically frequency and phase, to optimize the performance of quantum computation. The core mechanism involves a hierarchical feedback loop that continuously refines these parameters based on observed outcomes, resulting in enhanced qubit coherence and reduced error rates. This approach offers a significant advancement over traditional static control methods, potentially unlocking new capabilities within quantum computing. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the efficacy of this method in enhancing quantum coherence and exploring its impact on quantum algorithm complexity.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum Topology Expansion
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive quantum topology expansion algorithm designed to dynamically optimize quantum topology structures in response to system state changes. Traditional quantum topology optimization methods often rely on predefined topologies, hindering their ability to adapt to real-time variations. Our approach leverages machine learning to learn system states and automatically adjust quantum topology, enabling dynamic optimization and continuous monitoring and feedback. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through a series of simulations illustrating its adaptability and performance improvements compared to existing methods. The core mechanism involves a learning process that iteratively adjusts the quantum topology based on system feedback. This allows for a flexible and responsive optimization process, offering a significant advancement in the field of quantum topology.

abstract: Quantum State-Driven Machine Learning Knowledge Distillation is a novel approach to transfer knowledge from complex quantum machine learning models to simpler models. This research introduces a novel algorithm that leverages the unique properties of quantum states, specifically quantum superposition and entanglement, to facilitate knowledge migration and improve model generalization. The core mechanism involves mapping complex quantum states to simpler representations, effectively distilling the learned knowledge into a more manageable format. This work presents a robust and effective method for knowledge transfer, addressing limitations of traditional distillation techniques and offering a promising path towards enhanced model performance.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm, the "Multi-Scale Quantum Entanglement Mapping" (MSQEM), designed to model and compute complex topological information structures utilizing the inherent adaptability of quantum entanglement. Traditional approaches to topological information theory often struggle with intricate entangled states. The MSQEM leverages the self-adapting nature of quantum mechanics, specifically focusing on the mapping of quantum states, to create a framework for exploring and analyzing these systems. We present a detailed algorithm incorporating a novel mapping process, demonstrating its potential to generate more realistic and tractable topological models. The core claim is that this algorithm provides a robust and adaptable method for representing and manipulating multi-scale quantum entanglement, offering a significant advancement in the field. This work explores the implications of this approach for understanding fundamental quantum phenomena and potentially opens avenues for new topological information-based applications.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Networks
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics, holding the potential for revolutionary technologies in secure communication, quantum computing, and metrology. However, maintaining and manipulating entangled states is a significant challenge due to their fragility and susceptibility to decoherence. This paper explores the development of a novel quantum entanglement network utilizing a self-adaptive self-assembly mechanism. We propose a system where quantum entanglement networks are dynamically constructed and expanded through the application of "quantum pulses" – precisely modulated interactions designed to subtly alter the network's structure. This approach offers the potential for automatic network expansion and enhanced quantum information transfer, circumventing the limitations of traditional, manually designed architectures. The core mechanism revolves around the controlled manipulation of quantum entanglement through a carefully orchestrated sequence of pulses. This work demonstrates the feasibility of building a self-expanding entanglement network, highlighting the potential for significant advancements in quantum information processing.

title: Relational Reasoning with Graph Transformers and Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Graph transformers have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in processing graph-structured data, particularly in tasks like node classification and link prediction. However, a significant limitation remains their struggle with complex relational reasoning – the ability to understand intricate connections and dependencies between entities within a graph. This paper proposes a novel architecture that addresses this limitation by integrating graph transformers with knowledge graphs. Our approach leverages explicit relational embeddings derived from a structured knowledge graph to provide the transformer with a richer understanding of the relationships between nodes. We hypothesize that incorporating this knowledge will significantly improve the transformer's ability to perform sophisticated relational reasoning tasks. The core idea is to augment the standard graph transformer architecture with a mechanism that explicitly encodes relational information, thereby enhancing the model's capacity to infer and understand complex relationships within graph data. We evaluate our method on several benchmark graph reasoning datasets and demonstrate its superior performance compared to existing graph transformer models. The results validate the effectiveness of combining the strengths of graph transformers and knowledge graphs for enhanced relational understanding.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Causal Inference
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed causal inference leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional methods of causal inference face challenges in distributed systems, including latency, information silos, and difficulty in establishing robust causal relationships across geographically dispersed data sources. Our framework utilizes multiple quantum sensors to collect data from a distributed system. Quantum entanglement is then employed to correlate the measurement results from these sensors in real-time. This correlation is achieved through quantum entanglement-based quantum teleportation, facilitating the rapid propagation and synchronization of causal information. A causal inference model is constructed based on the characteristics of the entangled states, enabling real-time reasoning. The core claim is that this approach allows for real-time, high-precision inference of causal relationships in distributed systems, effectively addressing the limitations of conventional methods. We demonstrate the potential of exploiting quantum mechanics to achieve efficient causal inference in distributed environments.

We detail the core mechanism of QAPO, which centers around quantum entanglement and superposition to efficiently explore the parameter space and achieve optimal parameter configurations. The paper concludes with a discussion of the research's novelty, outlining the key contributions and future directions for this transformative approach.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement Modulation via Stochastic Feedback
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, is a profoundly fragile phenomenon, susceptible to decoherence. While classical techniques offer limited control, this paper proposes a novel method for manipulating and stabilizing entangled states using stochastic feedback. We introduce a quantum algorithm that continuously adjusts entanglement parameters based on a probabilistic feedback signal, aiming to mitigate decoherence and enhance fidelity. The core mechanism centers on a dynamically evolving feedback loop that leverages randomness to guide the state's evolution. This approach represents a fundamentally different strategy compared to existing classical control methods, potentially unlocking enhanced quantum communication and computation capabilities.

title: Distributed Fusion Filtering with Prediction Compensation for Multi-Sensor Systems Subject to DoS-Attack-Induced Packet Dropouts
abstract: This paper investigates the distributed fusion estimation problem for multi-sensor cyber-physical systems (CPSs), where the communication channels from local estimators to the fusion center are subject to random packet dropouts. Packet dropouts induced by either network congestion or intermittent denial-of-service (DoS) attacks are modeled as Bernoulli random variables. When a local estimate is lost, a prediction compensation strategy is adopted at the fusion center, where the missing data are replaced by their one-step predictors. By constructing an augmented state consisting of the original state, local prediction errors, and virtual measurements, the multi-sensor system is transformed into a stochastic system with random parameter matrices and one-step autocorrelated noises. Based on the transformed system, a distributed state fusion (DSF) filter is proposed via the innovation analysis method, whose filter gain depends on the successful-reception probabilities. The stability of the proposed DSF filter is analyzed, and a sufficient condition for the existence of a steady-state filter is obtained. The steady-state gain can be pre-computed offline, thereby reducing the online computational burden. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

title: Research data for Generation of fully phase controlled two-photon entangled states
abstract: The file contains all the data necessary to replicate the figures in the publication 'Generation of fully phase controlled two-photon entangled states'. The individual spreadsheets are for each figure with the data therein corresponding to the sub-figures, if applicable.AbstractControl over the internal states of trapped ions makes them the ideal system to generate single and two-photon states. Coupling a single ion to an optical cavity enables efficient emission of single photons into a single spatial mode and grants control over their temporal shape, phase, and frequency. Using the long coherence time of the ion’s internal states and employing a scheme to protect the coherence of the ion-cavity interaction, we demonstrate the generation of a two-photon entangled state with full control over the phase. Initially, ion-photon entanglement is generated. A second photon is subsequently generated, mapping the ion’s state onto the second photon. By adjusting the drive field the phase of the entangled state can be fully controlled. We implement this scheme in the most resource efficient way by utilizing a single 40Ca+ ion coupled to an optical cavity and demonstrate the generation of a two-photon entangled stated with full phase control with a fidelity of up to 82%.

title: A knowledge-aware graph-based framework for document-level event extraction
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of document-level event extraction as a critical step toward automated knowledge acquisition for intelligent systems. Extracting structured event knowledge from unstructured text is essential for downstream knowledge-based applications such as knowledge graph construction, decision support, and intelligent question answering. However, existing approaches struggle to effectively capture long-range dependencies and complex inter-event relationships within documents while maintaining computational efficiency. To address these challenges, we propose a novel knowledge-aware framework, the Graph Convolutional Network with Pseudo-trigger Combination Recognition(GCN-PCR). The proposed model explicitly represents entities, mentions, and sentences as interconnected nodes in a relational graph, enabling structured modeling of semantic dependencies and co-reference information across document contexts. Furthermore, the pseudo-trigger combination strategy enhances the identification of event structures by improving the robustness of event boundary detection and argument association. Extensive experiments on two public datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. More importantly, our framework provides a scalable and effective solution for transforming unstructured textual data into structured event knowledge, facilitating its integration into knowledge-based systems.

title: Quantum-enhanced hybrid-model compression using knowledge distillation
abstract: Abstract Quantum computing has emerged as a promising paradigm for addressing computational tasks intractable for classical systems, leveraging quantum mechanical principles such as superposition and entanglement to efficiently explore high-dimensional solution spaces. In recent years, hybrid quantum-classical approaches have gained increasing attention as a means to exploit the representational power of quantum systems while preserving the practicality of classical machine learning frameworks. This paper presents a study on quantum-enhanced model compression via feature-based knowledge distillation, in which a large classical neural network (the teacher) transfers knowledge to a substantially smaller hybrid student model. The proposed hybrid quantum-classical student architecture incorporates a parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) implemented in Qiskit, employing a linear $$\varvec{R_y}$$ angle-encoding feature map followed by an EfficientSU2 variational ansatz, with features bounded through a $$\varvec{\tanh (\cdot )\times \frac{\pi }{2}}$$ scaling to ensure stable gradient propagation. Gradient computation is performed via Reverse-Mode (adjoint) differentiation through the StatevectorEstimator primitive, which provides exact, shot-noise-free gradients at the cost of a single forward–backward pass per optimization step. The hybrid student is compared against a parameter-matched purely classical student under strict 1:1 parameter parity across a six-task binary benchmark spanning MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, as well as a four-class multi-class benchmark, totaling eleven classification experiments. A hardware validation experiment is additionally conducted on the IQM Garnet 20-qubit quantum processor using the Parameter-Shift Rule. The results indicate that the hybrid student outperforms its classical counterpart in five of six binary tasks (83%) and in the two hardest multi-class configurations, with advantages most pronounced in high-confusion regimes where compact classical classifiers approach the limits of their expressive capacity. On real quantum hardware, accuracy decreases from 99.04% in noiseless simulation to 80.50%, reflecting the impact of gate noise, readout errors, and transpilation overhead. While the hybrid model demonstrates improved parameter efficiency and expressive capacity, it incurs higher computational overhead and exhibits greater epoch-to-epoch training variability relative to classical baselines. We discuss practical limitations related to noise, scalability, and current hardware constraints, and identify directions for future work including hardware-efficient gradient estimation and advanced error mitigation protocols. Overall, our findings suggest that variational quantum circuits can serve as compact yet expressive components within neural compression schemes, with their representational advantage most effectively realized in binary and high-ambiguity classification scenarios.

title: Evaluation of MLLM-Agnostic Plug-and-Play Keyframe Selection Methods for Long Video Understanding
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) cannot process every frame of a long video because of limitations in visual-token and computational budgets. Three primary approaches have been proposed to enhance their long-video understanding capabilities: (i) Retraining an MLLM on a large video corpus and/or extending its input length; (ii) Training an adapter for a specific MLLM that takes the entire video and the query as input and selects the most relevant video frames; and (iii) Developing a training-free, plug-and-play (PaP) adapter that is MLLM-agnostic. We refer to the third approach as PaP keyframe selection. A PaP method may use only candidate video frames without considering the query, or it may use both candidate video frames and the query. The first approach is prohibitively expensive. The second approach requires substantial training time and computational resources, but it is accessible to many because an adapter contains significantly fewer trainable parameters than an entire MLLM. The third approach has the lowest computational cost and is therefore broadly accessible. To the best of our knowledge, only five PaP methods have been reported within the past year. All of these methods have been evaluated on one or more video question-answering benchmarks and have demonstrated improvements in long-video understanding. However, the methods were evaluated on different benchmarks using different MLLMs. We present a comprehensive evaluation of these five methods using three MLLMs across three long-video understanding benchmarks. Our results show that QAaF achieves the best performance in 13 of the 15 aggregate evaluation settings, while FOCUS ranks second overall. These results provide a common experimental reference for comparing training-free keyframe-selection methods for MLLMs.

title: Measured Sliders: Learning Continuous Controls from Differentiable Image Measurements
abstract: Continuous sliders are useful only when coefficient changes produce predictable image changes. Yet most diffusion sliders derive their axes from text or learned representations, leaving their scales disconnected from observable image properties. Consequently, we cannot tell in advance which attributes are learnable, compare control strengths directly, or anticipate interference when multiple controls are combined. We propose Measured Sliders, a framework that defines continuous controls through closed-form differentiable image measurements. A common measurement space unifies the pipeline. Before training, an observability test identifies usable supervision. During training, a measurement-guided objective learns target movement while suppressing non-target changes. After training, decoded calibration expresses controls in comparable units of realized image change. Multiple LoRA branches are stored in one checkpoint and composed without training on joint activations. Across SDXL and FLUX.1-dev, the resulting controls are ordered, selective, and composable. On 553 prompts, lighting direction reaches rho = 0.995 and 98.9% monotone sweeps. A five-attribute checkpoint achieves average selectivity 2.59, compared with 1.50 for the strongest baseline, and preserves every requested direction in 96.7% of pair and 86.1% of triple compositions. The observability test also separates every subsequently successful measurement from the failed candidate. Overall, image-space measurement provides a common basis for learning, diagnosing, calibrating, and composing continuous generative controls.

title: MCPO: Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Compression
abstract: Recently, multimodal large-scale reasoning models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in solving complex tasks through long Chains-of-Thought (M-CoT). However, excessively long reasoning trajectories incur substantial computational costs and significant KV-cache pressure. Existing CoT compression and alignment paradigms mainly rely on static rules or single-dimensional preferences, lacking fine-grained cross-modal constraints; as a result, they are prone to inducing visual laziness and hallucinatory reasoning. To address these issues, we propose Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization (MCPO), a highly sample-efficient two-stage length-compression method that requires fewer than 900 training samples. In the compression stage, we introduce a step-level Normalized Cross-Modal Mutual Information (NCMI) pruning algorithm, which automatically identifies and removes visual-independent reasoning steps by comparing the reasoning discrepancies between with-image and no-image contexts. This significantly reduces redundancy and hallucinatory content in the reasoning chains. In the alignment stage, the model first undergoes supervised fine-tuning to achieve domain-adaptive initialization, followed by optimization using an asymmetric multimodal length-controlled preference loss. This objective adopts a highly nonlinear odds-ratio formulation that provides steep gradients in the with-image context to reinforce length constraints for preferred trajectories, while applying a scaled, flat-gradient linear difference in the no-image context to maintain modality consistency, thereby achieving stable cross-modal preference alignment. Extensive experiments on mainstream base models such as Qwen3-VL-Thinking show that our method can reduce CoT length by up to 69.5% and achieve up to 3.34x end-to-end inference speedup while preserving original accuracy.

title: Designing Production-Grade Agentic AI for Continuous Payment Exception Monitoring, Hierarchical Authorization, and Governance in Financial Systems: An MCP, LLM, and RAG Implementation Architecture
abstract: Autonomous AI systems for financial payment operations have matured from theoretical governance proposals to deployable production architectures, yet the published literature has not kept pace with the tooling ecosystem that makes such systems practically viable. This paper advances the state of the art in two directions. First, it formalizes a production-grade agentic AI framework for continuous payment exception monitoring and hierarchical authorization, grounding the governance model in a parent-child agent architecture that coordinates risk assessment, revenue impact scoring, and customer relationship evaluation before any exception resolution action is taken. Second — and as the primary new contribution of this revision — it specifies a concrete implementation architecture in which the agentic AI system operates through Model Context Protocol (MCP) server/client connections, a large language model (LLM) reasoning core, and a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline that grounds every autonomous decision in a continuously refreshed corpus of regulatory policy, internal governance rules, and historical resolution precedents. The MCP-mediated architecture allows the agentic AI system to query payment data, compliance documents, customer relationship records, and revenue analytics through standardized tool interfaces — without requiring custom integration code for each data source. The RAG pipeline ensures that the LLM reasoning core grounds its exception analysis in specific, citable regulatory text rather than parametric knowledge, producing verifiable and audit-ready reasoning chains. A production deployment on a payment processing platform handling 2.3 million monthly transactions demonstrates a 99.7% reduction in mean time to resolve auto-eligible exceptions, an 89% ACH recovery rate, a 43% reduction in analyst workload, and zero compliance audit findings over a 12-month post-deployment window. These results demonstrate that MCP-mediated, RAG-grounded agentic AI is not a research prototype capability — it is a deployable production architecture for the financial services industry today.

title: Decision Confidence Neuron in Echo State Network for Continual Evaluation of EEG Motor Imagery Classification Quality
abstract: Abstract Echo state networks (ESNs) are efficient, neuro-inspired computational frameworks well suited to time-series data. However, ESN decision confidence is typically quantified in limited ways. We propose an explicit decision-confidence readout neuron, trained from decision readout outputs, to continuously monitor confidence as decisions form. In a simulated decision task, confidence activity increased with stimulus strength, linking greater discriminability to higher confidence. We then evaluated the model on EEG-based motor imagery classification, showing that confidence activity increased with decision accuracy and discriminated correct from error decisions, particularly in higher-performing participants, reflecting human-like metacognition. Overall, this approach enables continual monitoring of decision confidence, supporting more trustworthy ESN decisions, particularly in biomedical applications.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Non-Linear Feature Selection
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) offers a paradigm shift in machine learning by leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to enhance computational capabilities and model accuracy. This paper explores a novel approach to feature selection, termed "Quantum Feature Selection" (QFS), that utilizes quantum entanglement to establish a non-linear relationship between data features and model outputs. We propose a method predicated on the inherent properties of quantum states, aiming to improve the performance of machine learning models by introducing a novel form of feature representation. The core claim of this work is that QFS can achieve superior performance compared to traditional feature selection techniques through the application of quantum entanglement and non-linear modeling.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Potential Field Simulation
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to quantum potential field simulation, leveraging adaptive quantum field parameter adjustment to achieve more accurate and efficient simulations. Traditional methods rely on manual parameter tuning, while this framework utilizes a dynamic adjustment mechanism to automatically optimize the simulation for complex quantum systems. The core of the innovation lies in a self-adjusting system that continuously monitors the system's behavior and modifies the quantum field parameters accordingly, resulting in improved simulation fidelity and enhanced performance in quantum computing. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations, showcasing significant improvements in the representation of quantum phenomena compared to conventional methods. The paper highlights the benefits of automated parameter adjustment and its potential to accelerate the development of quantum algorithms.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Bayesian Optimization-Based Algorithm for Automated Model Parameter Tuning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum machine learning algorithm based on Bayesian optimization, designed to automatically adjust model parameters for optimal performance. Traditional machine learning model parameter optimization often relies on manual adjustments, which struggles to adapt to evolving data. Our algorithm leverages the probabilistic nature of model parameters, employing Bayesian optimization to dynamically refine the model, ultimately leading to improved accuracy and generalization. This work presents a fundamentally new approach to model parameter tuning, offering enhanced adaptability and potential for superior results compared to existing methods.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Aware Adaptive Quantum Computing Framework
abstract: Quantum entanglement-aware adaptive quantum computing frameworks represent a significant advancement in the field of quantum computation, addressing the limitations of static parameter design. This paper proposes a novel framework that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust quantum computation parameters, ultimately enhancing both computational efficiency and accuracy. The core mechanism revolves around exploiting entanglement to create a feedback loop, allowing the system to self-optimize and mitigate errors. This innovative approach offers a potential pathway towards more robust and versatile quantum algorithms.

title: topic-modeller: A Generic Multilingual Topic Modeling Pipeline
abstract: A generic, metadata-aware topic modeling pipeline built on BERTopic and transformer-based sentence embeddings. Accepts any CSV corpus with a text column and optional metadata (year, url, domain, id, etc.), identifies the main themes across the documents, and produces word clouds, bar charts, heatmaps and metadata breakdowns such as topic share over time or per domain. Supports multilingual corpora, adaptive settings for small and large datasets, batch processing of multiple corpora, and GPU acceleration.

title: Title: Algorithmic Emergence of Self-Organizing Structures
abstract: This paper explores the potential of algorithmic emergence to generate complex, fractal-like structures with inherent properties of self-replication and adaptation. We propose a novel design incorporating a genetic algorithm coupled with reinforcement learning to iteratively refine a structure, fostering self-organization and driving the creation of intricate patterns. The core mechanism centers on a feedback loop that governs the structure's evolution, promoting robustness and novelties. The current investigation highlights the importance of a carefully constructed feedback loop as a key component in achieving this emergent behavior. The research delves into the design of the algorithm to effectively leverage the strengths of both genetic algorithms and reinforcement learning, ultimately aiming to create structures with unpredictable yet controllable properties. The goal is to move beyond simple, pre-defined patterns towards a system capable of generating novel and complex forms through self-directed evolution.

title: Based on Quantum Coherence for Differentiable Neural Network Training
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to training neural networks by leveraging the concept of quantum coherence. The core idea is to incorporate quantum coherence as a differentiable signal to guide the optimization of neural network parameters. Traditional neural network training relies on gradient descent methods, which can suffer from limitations in convergence speed and local minima. We propose a framework where the change in quantum coherence is used as a proxy for the gradient, offering a potentially more efficient and robust training mechanism. This work demonstrates the theoretical feasibility of this method and outlines a core claim, mechanism, and the significance of introducing quantum mechanics into the realm of neural network training. The central focus is on establishing a differentiable link between quantum coherence and network parameter adjustments. This approach aims to overcome potential training bottlenecks inherent in conventional neural networks.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence: A Cognitive Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a cognitive architecture for explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), aiming to decompose AI decision-making processes into interpretable modules. The core mechanism centers around a cognitive science-inspired architecture, segmenting decisions into modules such as perception, memory, reasoning, and learning. Each module is designed to produce transparent outputs, enhancing the trustworthiness and understandability of AI systems. The architecture focuses on providing justifications for AI decisions, addressing a key challenge in current AI development – the "black box" problem. This work outlines the foundational elements of the architecture and discusses potential applications, emphasizing the importance of transparency and human-AI collaboration. The ultimate goal is to create AI systems that not only perform well but also offer clear and understandable explanations for their actions.

title: Title: Bayesian Geometric Modeling for Optimal Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian Geometric Modeling (BGM) framework for optimal algorithm design, addressing the limitations of traditional optimization methods. The core concept is to move beyond fixed parameter optimization and instead, build a probabilistic model of the problem space that dynamically adjusts algorithm parameters based on observed performance. This model utilizes Bayesian inference to iteratively refine the algorithm configuration, maximizing performance while maintaining robustness against changes in the problem environment. The framework incorporates a representation of the problem space, enabling the model to learn the optimal algorithm configuration through a process of probabilistic adjustment. This approach offers a more adaptive and robust approach to algorithm design compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios involving complex, non-stationary environments. The benefits of this framework include improved performance, increased adaptability, and a reduced reliance on explicit parameter tuning.

title: 基于量子拓扑的量子信息存储
abstract: Quantum information storage is a crucial area of research due to the increasing demand for robust and secure data. Traditional methods often rely on physical isolation, which limits scalability and security. This paper explores a novel approach leveraging quantum topology to design a fundamentally new quantum information storage architecture. We propose a quantum information storage system that utilizes the unique properties of quantum topology to optimize information storage. This system employs a sophisticated quantum algorithm to manage data, enhancing security and potentially increasing storage capacity compared to existing approaches. The core mechanism centers around the manipulation of quantum states through topological properties, resulting in a more resilient and secure storage paradigm. We detail the architecture, the optimization process, and the resulting security implications, presenting a framework for future advancements in quantum information technologies.

title: Hyperdimensional Geometric Modeling of Complex Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the application of a novel computational framework for creating highly detailed geometric representations of complex systems. We propose a 'Hyperdimensional Mapping' algorithm, leveraging quantum states to generate a 'virtual' 3D model of a system, enabling unprecedented levels of simulation fidelity and visualization. The core claim is that this method represents a significant step beyond traditional geometric modeling, offering a fundamentally new approach to complex system analysis and representation. This work focuses on the potential of quantum state manipulation to achieve a level of detail and computational efficiency unmatched by existing techniques. The paper will detail the algorithm's design, demonstrate its capabilities through specific examples, and discuss the implications for various fields, including physics, biology, and engineering.

title: A Generic Construction of Plateaued Functions via Support Modification of Quadratic Functions
abstract: Plateaued Boolean functions play an important role in sequence design and cryptography due to their favorable properties such as high nonlinearity, resilience and low additive autocorrelation. In this paper, by modifying the support of certain quadratic functions, we propose a generic construction of plateaued Boolean functions. Additionally, we analyze the algebraic normal form of the newly constructed functions. As applications of the proposed construction, we obtain infinite families of near-bent and semi-bent functions.

title: Hessian-Informed Conformation Augmentation for Potential Energy Surface Curvature in Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
abstract: While machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have successfully learned potential energy surfaces (PES) and atomic forces, many practical applications, such as vibrational analysis and transition state search, rely heavily on the PES Hessian. Yet standard MLIPs are trained on energy and forces only, and using the Hessian as an additional training objective requires backpropagation whose memory cost grows quadratically with the number of atoms. To address these limitations, we propose two Hessian-derived data augmentation schemes: isotropic Gaussian displacement (\textbf{UniAug}) and normal mode-weighted displacement (\textbf{ModeAug}). Both methods utilize simple Taylor expansions, generating physically grounded molecular structures with highly accurate energy and force labels. By preserving the underlying MLIP architecture and training procedure, this approach contributes to improving energy and force predictions in various benchmarks. Comprehensive evaluations across non-equilibrium and equilibrium datasets demonstrate that our approach enhances model accuracy where reference forces are large and training data are limited.
